question: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician for a physical examination prior to participating in sports. She has no history of serious illness. She is on the school's cheerleading team and is preparing for an upcoming competition. Menarche was at 13 years of age, and her last menstrual period was 4 months ago. She is 167 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (99 lb); BMI is 16.1 kg/m2. Examination shows pale skin with thin, soft body hair. The patient is at increased risk for which of the following complications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Low BMI" -> "underweight" -> "nutritional deficiency" -> "decreased bone density" -> "increased risk of fractures" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Amenorrhea" -> "hormonal imbalance" -> "decreased estrogen" -> "decreased bone density" -> "increased risk of fractures" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pale skin" -> "possible anemia" -> "nutritional deficiency" -> "decreased bone density" -> "increased risk of fractures" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Thin, soft body hair" -> "possible malnutrition" -> "decreased bone density" -> "increased risk of fractures" -> 80%
analysis: The patient exhibits signs consistent with an eating disorder, such as low BMI, amenorrhea, and lanugo (thin, soft body hair). These symptoms suggest a condition like anorexia nervosa, which is associated with an increased risk of osteoporosis due to low body weight and hormonal imbalances. This makes her more susceptible to fractures.
